messages:
Olivia: Quick sync — ACME Dedicated commit sizing. They want predictability for SLAs but traffic is super bursty (short spikes from batch jobs + steady background). Need a recommended committed throughput for eu-west-1. Any obs?
Sam: Do we have 30d utilization buckets? IIRC their 95th is way above mean because of nightly spikes.
Maria: I pulled a 30d rolling window this morning. Avg sustained ~= 12 vGPUs (p95 ~ 22), but observed bursts up to 48 for 10-25m, ~6 events in last 30d.
Jake: Important: bursts correlate with a nightly ETL kicking off from customer side. They can change schedule but likely want contract that won't bill them insane overages.
Olivia: Two tradeoffs: 1) commit to p95 sustained (~22) + configured burst buffer (reserved burst pool) OR 2) commit to baseline (12) + pre-agreed burst credits (banked hours) that auto-top up. Thoughts on billing ops feasibility? :thinking:
billing-bot: ACME usage summary: 30d avg=12.1, p95=22.4, max=48.0, burst_events(>30vGPU)=6. Link: https://billing.internal/acme/usage/30d
Sam: Option 2 seems fairer for them. We can model burst credits as prepaid hours used at committed rate; excess billed at on-demand. Ops question: can we guarantee latency if they burst into shared capacity? We need a backstop.
Maria: From infra side: we can offer 'guaranteed baseline' on-dedicated nodes + 'best-effort burst pool' across AZs. Guaranteed baseline = 12 vGPUs isolated. For bursts we can route to regional shared capacity with fallback to smaller quantized model variants to keep 99th latency under SLA.
Jake: Network constraint: eu-west-1 has ephemeral NIC limits on our smallest racks. If they hit 48 vGPUs, we need to ensure network bandwidth and placement spread. That's additional ops cost.
Olivia: Proposal draft: Commit = 15 vGPUs reserved (gives margin over avg); burst credits = 2000 vGPU-min prepaid per month (covers ~33m at 48 vGPUs), overage at on-demand. SLA tiers: baseline backed by reserved pool, bursts best-effort with preferential queuing and model-fallthrough.
Sam: Quick calc — commit 15 at price X => ~monthly commit cost C. If they prefer lower up-front, allow 12 commit + 3000 burst credits. Need finance to show modeled bills under 3 scenarios.
Olivia: Maria/Jake can you estimate incremental infra cost to support bursts (cross-AZ traffic, extra NIC capacity, ops on-call) as a monthly delta? Also need rollback policy if burst pattern becomes sustained.
Maria: I'll run a placement simulation and ops-impact estimate today. Will post outputs here.
Jake: I'll check rack network headroom and whether we need to pre-provision trunked NICs for eu-west. If we do, one-time config + ongoing cost.
Olivia: Also flagging contract wording: define "burst credits" redemption logic and expiration. @billing-bot can you produce 3 pricing scenarios (commit 12/15/20 + varying burst credits) and include projected invoice for last 90 days?
billing-bot: Generating scenarios. ETA ~20m.
Sam: For rollout plan, recommend 30d canary: commit at 15 for 30d on a soft contract, monitor throttle events and cost delta, then finalize 12-month commit if stable.
Olivia: Perfect. Action items: Maria run placement & ops-cost; Jake validate network; billing-bot produce price scenarios; Sam draft canary measurement checklist (latency, throttle, billing). I'll circle back to ACME PM after we have numbers. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Note: canary flag 'acme_commit_test' created and will auto-instrument traces and token-level cost for 30d.
Maria: Posting preliminary placement results in 30m — early takeaway: to accommodate 48 vGPUs bursts without cross-AZ degradation we'd need to reserve two racks in eu-west or accept model-splitting fallback.
Olivia: Good. If placement cost is too high, fallback is to keep commit low and provide robust fallback model variants for bursts. We'll aim to present options tomorrow.
Jake: +1. I'll update once NIC checks complete.
Olivia: Thanks all — sync later today 4pm PT if needed.
